propositions: Rebar's current structured-output seams (deterministic repair, schema extraction, three-attempt ceiling, stop-reason fast-fail, derived budgets, durable usage telemetry) must be preserved or explicitly decided as intentional deltas when replacing with Pydantic AI 1.107.2 primitives.

The offline integration probe exercises real Pydantic Agent, output retry, fallback, limits, and hooks seams without live model calls, verifying 32 declared observations including successful/exhausted retry, request/token/tool limits, fallback predicates, truncation handling, and usage aggregation against 19 approved decisions.

Seven Phase-4 maintainer decisions were approved: one operation-wide request budget; complete failed response on proven fit or whole omission; bounded output-size retry with concise guidance; terminal refusal/content-filter; aggregate successful-run usage; exact cause-chain exception restoration; and trace-event (not usage-field) candidate observability.

Behavioral contract reconstruction maps 16 deduplicated scenarios against 15 historical ticket aliases plus ADR 0056, with 290 passing tests across 13 source suites providing current-Rebar authority and 407 total passing tests validating core regressions.

Material intentional deltas require explicit maintainer approval before ticketization: successful retry aggregates all attempt tokens into one row (not accepted-attempt-only); exhaustion re-raises exact Rebar-owned error from cause chain (not blanket translation); fallback candidates emit trace events (not synthetic usage fields).
Implementation ticketization is deferred to the pydantic-ai lane (story 155c); this research task is complete and all acceptance criteria are operator-attested with no code changes to tracked files.
